title: Jáuregui’s Defense Demands That Mexico’s Attorney General Summon Governor Maru Campos to Say What She Knows About the CIA
author: Sugeyry Romina Gándara
content:
_This article by[Sugeyry Romina
Gándara](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/sugeyry_gandara/) originally
appeared in the [October 21, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4891058/la-defensa-de-jauregui-exige-a-
fgr-citar-a-maru-para-que-diga-lo-que-sabe-de-la-cia/), an independent Mexican
digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 21 (SinEmbargo).–** Former prosecutor **César Gustavo
Jáuregui Moreno** was formally charged with the crime of **Treason** , as a
co-perpetrator and for allegedly intentional conduct. The [**Federal Attorney
General 's Office (FGR)**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/fgr/) maintains that
the former official consented to, authorized, and allowed the presence of two
foreign individuals in the operation carried out in **El Pinal** , in the
municipality of **Morelos** ,
[**Chihuahua**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/chihuahua/), thereby allegedly
putting at risk the sovereignty and independence of **Mexico** by attempting
to subject the country to a foreign government.

However, **Jáuregui 's** defense asserts that there is no solid, video, or
documentary evidence proving his participation. It also argues that, under the
same logic with which the [**Attorney General 's
Office**](https://www.fgr.org.mx/) seeks to attribute responsibility to the
former prosecutor, the **Governor of Chihuahua** , **María Eugenia Campos
Galván** , must also be investigated to determine what she knew about the
operation and whether she bore any responsibility. For the defense, it is even
imperative that the state governor be called to testify.

> "If we are going to enter that terrain, then it would also be necessary to
> investigate whether the head of the Executive had knowledge of the
> operation," attorney Héctor Villasana said in an interview with
> **SinEmbargo** , after the hearing for the formulation of charges, which
> lasted at least eight hours.

For the attorney, who is part of the former prosecutor's defense team, the
Governor's public statements, made on October 14 on _Latinus_ , in which she
held Jáuregui and other officials of the state prosecutor's office responsible
for acting without her knowledge, make it necessary for the FGR to take her
testimony and contrast her versions with the other elements of the
investigation.

> "I think what the Attorney General's Office would have to do is summon the
> Governor, as a result of these statements she made, in which she changed her
> version, and make her appear through the mechanisms," Villasana said.

![Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos speaks at a podium at a 'Yo con Maru'
event](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jauregui-
defense-maru-cia-maru-podium.jpg)César Jáuregui's defense asked that Maru
Campos, Governor of Chihuahua, be summoned to testify about the presence of
the CIA in the state. Photo: Cuartoscuro

The attorney noted that, as far as he knew, Campos Galván had not testified
before the FGR regarding the presence of agents of the United States (US)
Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) in the operation in the Sierra Tarahumara.
He recalled that she was summoned on May 27, but did not give a statement
because, as was reported at the time, she questioned the conditions of the
summons.

The defense also considered that the investigation must look more deeply into
the chain of command and into what the various officials may have known about
the participation of the foreigners. Nevertheless, Villasana insisted that the
charge against Jáuregui is not supported, from his perspective, by evidence
showing that he authorized or consented to the presence of the agents.

> "The concrete thing here is that the accusation against Prosecutor César
> Jáuregui is not based on any piece of evidence that concludes that he
> participated in, consented to, or authorized the presence of these people,"
> he stressed.

## The Hearing: 150 Pieces of Evidence Presented

The charge against Jáuregui is based, according to what his attorney set out,
on Article 123, section I, of the Federal Penal Code, which covers the crime
of Treason.

During the hearing, the FGR presented **close to 150 pieces of evidence** ,
including witness statements, expert opinions, and analyses. The Attorney
General's Office says that the then head of the Chihuahua State Attorney
General's Office (FGE) allowed the presence of two foreign individuals in the
operation against an alleged drug lab in El Pinal.

![Former Chihuahua prosecutor César Jáuregui surrounded by
reporters](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/jauregui-
defense-maru-cia-jauregui.jpg)César Jáuregui, former prosecutor of Chihuahua,
is accused of the crime of Treason. Photo: Manuel Sánchez, Cuartoscuro

The accusation argues that, with that conduct, Jáuregui put at risk the
sovereignty and independence of the Republic by attempting to subject it to a
foreign government.

Villasana explained that the Attorney General's Office attributes to his
client an intentional participation and as a co-perpetrator, not a
responsibility derived solely from an omission.

> "No, no, no. The accusation is as intentional and as co-perpetrator. He came
> to an agreement. That is, co-perpetration implies that there is a prior
> concert and agreement between the parties to commit a crime. So that is how
> the accusation stands," he clarified.

## They Point to the Deceased Director of the AEI

The defense strategy, according to what the attorney laid out, will focus on
maintaining that, so far, all the evidence presented by the FGR indicates that
the direct relationship with the U.S. agents belonged solely to Pedro Román
Oseguera Cervantes, then director of the State Investigation Agency (AEI).

Oseguera Cervantes was one of the four people who died in the rollover that
occurred in Polanco, after the deployment related to the operation.

It should be noted that among the elements presented by the FGR's Public
Prosecutor were some of the reports submitted by Wendy Chávez, head of the
Specialized Unit that Maru Campos created to investigate the case.

In this regard, it is important to recall that on May 12, in a second report
of the state investigation, it was stated that **CIA agents had visited the
facilities of the Strategic Operations Prosecutor 's Office at least twice**,
including hours before the operation, and that one of them was carrying a
firearm.

Villasana stated that the photographic records and witness statements place
the foreigners at the facilities of the State Investigation Agency and not at
the central offices of the Attorney General's Office, where Jáuregui worked.

> "The entire investigation concludes that the meetings and the visits and the
> presence of these people took place at the offices of the General
> Directorate of the State Investigation Agency. The State Investigation
> Agency is about 10 kilometers away, it is on the way out of the city of
> Chihuahua [the exit to Ciudad Aldama], and the central offices of the
> Attorney General's Office, where the Attorney General works, are downtown,
> right next to the Government Palace," he clarified.

Based on these elements, the defense maintains that it must be clarified who
coordinated the presence of the agents, which officials maintained
communication with them, and who had knowledge of their participation in the
operation.

> "So, never, there is no piece of evidence, there is no video, there is no
> log, there is absolutely nothing that proves there was a meeting between Mr.
> Jáuregui and these people," he stated.

The attorney insisted that the investigation must look more deeply into the
conduct of those who, according to the evidence presented, had contact with
the foreign agents.

> It will be up to the Attorney General's Office to investigate whether, under
> this same scheme of omission, the Governor could bear serious
> responsibility.
>
> Héctor Villasana, Jáuregui's defense attorney

As for former prosecutor Guillermo Zuany, Villasana said that participation is
also attributed to him for having been director of Operations of the Strategic
Operations Unit.

The attorney indicated that Zuany maintained communication with Oseguera
Cervantes, since he had recently left the Directorate of the State
Investigation Agency, after the Governor appointed him head of the Strategic
Operations Unit and designated Oseguera as director of the Agency.

> "The meetings between them are, in a way, logical and understandable for
> following up on pending matters in this transition," he noted.

After a hearing that lasted at least eight hours, the defense requested the
doubling of the constitutional term to prepare its arguments before it is
determined whether Jáuregui will be bound over for trial.

The Judge set the continuation of the hearing for Saturday at 3:00 p.m.
Because the crime charged carries mandatory pretrial detention, **the former
prosecutor must remain in jail** while his legal situation is resolved,
according to what his attorney said.

## Judge Submitted Her Resignation

Villasana also confirmed that the arrest warrant against the former Chihuahua
prosecutor, César Jáuregui Moreno, was issued by federal Judge Mariana Vieyra
Valdez, assigned to the Federal Criminal Justice Center of Almoloya de Juárez,
who, as was reported during the hearing, had submitted her resignation.
